29:**The player-facing effect.** The player meets it as the ship's own voice, read by their own light. A gauge on a wall is readable exactly as far as the beam, a fixture, a lantern pool or a Chemlight glowstick reaches it ("What You Light, You Can Read"); the needle sits in a zone band coded by pattern as well as hue, with no numerals at game-camera distance; the player reads cause, mass and rest at a glance (a needle that steps to a new reading and comes to rest, and eases heavily when the change is a real jump; a needle that shakes under real stress) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* and learns the one motion that has no cause, no mass and no rest: the lie. When precision matters they stand still in their own light and press `inspect`: a card appears beside the instrument carrying its label, the same needle and zone band, and one numeral with its unit — never a state word or a verdict. The card is the same instrument, not a second one: it lies exactly when its wall gauge lies (advisor ruling R13), so inspecting is a precision tool and never a free falsifier. The real check is always a different reading elsewhere or the consequence channel the Graph and Failure & Trail draw (frost, drip, draught, hiss, breath, a rotor's sound).
55:| P1 The World Never Lies | "Only instruments and perception can be wrong." Design test: "a hidden stat vs. a visibly leaking pipe -> the pipe" | reads a gauge, then confirms it against frost, drip, breath, draught or a rotor's sound; the instrument is the one thing allowed to be wrong |
89:**Beat B: the first lie (stage 1, `engine_room`, the home loop running fault-free).** The first lie in any world is FALSE_FAIL or GLIDE on a fault-free lit subject with all three leak modes (SN-16). The oxygen-partial-pressure dial `inst_engine_room_p_o2` reads NORMAL; the home loop is running, fault-free. About ten seconds after the player enters, the needle begins to slide toward the alarm side with nothing in the room to explain it, never resting (at an 18 art px needle the Filter's `rate_floor` is 1.59 deg/s, PF-17, so about 16 degrees in 10 s); a thin violet fringe (`#B07BE6`, never the core `#8A3FD1`) sits on the glass edge; a faint wrong-pitched tick sounds (`FA_LIE_SIG_GAUGE`, PF-20). Each mode alone is sufficient (HR-5). The player opens the card and **the card glides too**, with the same gleam: precision did not save them (R13). They check the cheapest truth: their own breath, the room's witness, a second reading (`suit.o2` for the room they stand in, which counts because the first lie is ALARM-direction, or another compartment's gauge, SN-15 L-2I) or a `field_check` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; BLOCKING 1)*. The lie returns to truth on the glide path, unannounced, identically whether it expired or was debunked; the game never says "that was a hallucination". *Feeling:* a cold prickle, then the satisfaction of catching it with the world. P4 test: "a hallucination that can never be disproved vs. one that costs time, risk or trust to disprove -> the costly one."
398:*Edge notes.* Accessibility Settings (Alpha) depends on this GDD (IDX:209): its reduced-motion toggle reads the Filter's published scalars (`reduced_motion_glide_pm`, `breath_depth_pm`, `lie_tick_min_ms`) and this rule's substitute *(provisional — Accessibility Settings undesigned)*. The screen-reader text for a card (Alpha) is built from `Perceived.displayed_value` only, never `true_value`; the pinned engine's accessibility live-region maturity is `[UNV]`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Tell survival for a deaf, colour-blind player.** With the sound removed and the hue removed, a lie keeps the never-rest motion mode on the needle, the continuous tick on the card numeral and the gleam as a **luminance** fringe; the claim of at least two tells therefore holds only if the fringe `#B07BE6` keeps at least `GLEAM_LUM_CONTRAST_MIN` 3:1 (the WCAG non-text ratio, `[PLACEHOLDER]`) against the glass it rides in greyscale, measured at S-A1 and tested by AC-IW-120. **Tell-survival rule** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: for every combination of reduced motion (scale 0.6), captions on or off, greyscale or a colour-vision filter, and sound off, at least two of the three tells survive on every lying instrument: the never-resting needle (the wander is never scaled, PF-39), the luminance gleam (above `GLEAM_LUM_CONTRAST_MIN`) and the sound (not counted when sound is off or unheard). The numeral tick is a mode of the motion tell and is not counted as a separate tell. Where reduced motion lengthens a digit hold, D.12 accepts it explicitly (`T_VIS_MAX_RM_S`). Tested by AC-IW-125; the caption tier is recorded in `design/accessibility-requirements.md` once that file exists (OQ-IW-42). 15:- R1 Restore epoch (consequence of X8/D16). Save/Load OWNS `restore_epoch` as a persisted integer in the save slot header (u32, starts 0). On every restore (death restart or load), Save/Load increments it and durably writes the header (atomic header-only write) BEFORE the first RUNNING tick, so reloading the same autosave twice, in-process or after a fresh process start, gives a new epoch each time. The kernel exposes it read-only in `kernel.clock` as (T, world_seed, restore_epoch) — sim-visible, pure. The KERNEL (command-simulation-layer.md) owns the one derivation for threat draws, counter_eff = rng_counter + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE x restore_epoch, and owns RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE (value 1048576 unchanged; registry_request: move its source from attention-system.md to command-simulation-layer.md, with attention, horror and save-load in referenced_by). The stream name hash stays cached and unchanged. Attention and Horror call the kernel derivation; neither defines its own. Graph physical failures and persisted counters never read the epoch. Determinism (G3/G4) is defined given (save bytes, restore_epoch): the same pair replays identically; tests pin the epoch. Required ACs: (i) two successive restores of the same save yield epochs e and e+1 and different threat draws; (ii) a fresh-process reload of the same slot also advances the epoch; (iii) same (save, epoch) pair -> identical draws. Save/Load's 'none of it able to alter the sim' is amended to exempt restore_epoch.
22:- R8 Units of a request field shared by producer and consumer (e.g. Perception LEVEL vs Audio): G1 — the producer defines the unit; the consumer converts. State the unit in both GDDs with the conversion.

Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: PowerShell 7+ (pwsh)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` ARE available and work like bash. Prefer `cmd1 && cmd2` over `cmd1; cmd2` when cmd2 should only run if cmd1 succeeds.
   - Ternary (`$cond ? $a : $b`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are available.
   - Default file encoding is UTF-8 without BOM.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__edit_version
tools.description: Publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit (some clients refuse any artifact but your own as owner-only), by replacing text in its current document: use it for a small change instead of sending the whole page to publish_version. The server reads the live index.html, applies every edit in order, and publishes the result as one new version; if any edit cannot be applied, nothing is published. Each old_text must occur exactly once in the document as it stands when that edit is applied: include enough surrounding text to make it unique. base_version must name the live version (from get_artifact, read_artifact, list_files or your last publish result); if it is no longer live the call is rejected with a conflict that names the live version: read what you are changing again and retry. To rename the artifact pass title, which also rewrites the document's <title> element; an edit to that element without title is refused, because the server keeps it in step with the artifact's title. Artifacts that contain a live (collaboratively edited) document cannot be edited here. An artifact made from a type is edited only if this server offers list_files, and only with path: one of its own text files, as list_files lists them, never its page or its type's files.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_files
tools.description: Publish an artifact from files on disk: their bytes go from the files to the artifact and do not pass through you. Prefer this to publish_version when the page's files already exist, when there is more than one file or an image, or when the page is large. For each file give `as`, the path it is served at, and `path`, its absolute path on the machine where your own file tools run; leave `uri` out. index.html is required in a new artifact. Limits for one call: 256 files, 20 MiB a file, 64 MiB in all. The client may refuse a file it will not send, such as a secrets file, a link or a path outside the working folder. Omit slug to create an artifact, private to you. To republish, give slug and base_version (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish); title and icon are kept when omitted. A republish changes only the files named and keeps the rest, which stay served: to take a file away, list it in remove. mode "replace" makes the files named the whole artifact and drops the rest. This tool publishes only to an artifact of yours. **Files Claude did not write**: Claude reads the whole file before publishing it, even when the person asks it not to. Publishing distributes the content, and Claude never distributes what it has not seen. A request for privacy is a reason to read before publishing, not an exemption. If Claude cannot read the file, it does not publish it. **Claude never publishes** a page that impersonates a real person or organization, for example by using their name, branding, byline or domain. Claude also never publishes fabricated records, receipts or reviews presented as genuine, forms or flows that collect credentials or payment details under false pretenses, or content that targets a private individual. Claude refuses whether it wrote the page or the person supplied it, and whatever purpose is claimed, such as a prop or a test, when the page would work as the real thing. If publishing is refused, Claude does not suggest other ways to host or share the page.

artifact_title.description: The artifact's current title, as get_artifact gives it. Needed when shared_live is 'public'.

contract.description: Optional runtime-contract version. Leave it out to keep the current one.

Required when that value is 'users' (named people or groups), 'org' (the user's whole organization) or 'public' (anyone with the link). Leave it out for a new artifact and when the value is 'owner'. slug.description: The artifact's slug. Omit to create a new artifact.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_version
tools.description: Publish an artifact: either create a new artifact — omit slug and give title and content; you become its owner and it starts private to you — or publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit — give slug and base_version. Some clients may publish only to your own artifacts: there the call is refused as owner-only. Republishing is read-then-send: base_version must name the live version you are replacing (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result) — if it is no longer live, the publish is rejected with a conflict; re-read and retry from the current state. On success the new version goes live immediately. When republishing, the artifact's stored connectors manifest carries forward unchanged, and so do title, favicon, icon and contract when omitted. Content is capped at 16 MiB.

schema.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_version
schema.description: Publish an artifact: either create a new artifact — omit slug and give title and content; you become its owner and it starts private to you — or publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit — give slug and base_version. Some clients may publish only to your own artifacts: there the call is refused as owner-only. Republishing is read-then-send: base_version must name the live version you are replacing (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result) — if it is no longer live, the publish is rejected with a conflict; re-read and retry from the current state. On success the new version goes live immediately. When republishing, the artifact's stored connectors manifest carries forward unchanged, and so do title, favicon, icon and contract when omitted. Content is capped at 16 MiB.

artifact_title.description: The artifact's current title, as get_artifact gives it. Needed when shared_live is 'public'.

base_version.description: Required when slug is given: the version id this publish replaces — echo the version get_artifact or read_artifact returned (or your last publish result's). Rejected with a conflict if it no longer names the live version, so concurrent edits are never silently overwritten. Omit when creating.

content.description: The complete HTML document, at most 16 MiB. Must sniff as text/html — begin it with <!DOCTYPE html>.

contract.description: Optional runtime-contract version (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). Leave it out to keep the current one. Pass one only when the user asks for a different version, or this server's answer says to. If the publish is rejected because the contract is yanked or out of the supported window, republish with an explicit "0.0.0" to clear the contract — omitting the argument is not a reliable recovery (the server may carry the stored contract forward, repeating the rejection).

deadline.description: Optional, rarely needed: by when pages still open on an OLDER version must have moved to this one — one word: now, 15m, 1h, 24h, 7d, or an ISO-8601 time at most 30 days ahead. Omit it for ordinary edits (open pages then move at their next quiet moment); it cannot be relaxed once published.

favicon.description: Optional legacy emoji marker; omit it.

icon.description: One short, generic word for the artifact's tab icon — a plain signifier of what it is, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map; not a product or brand name. Pass one when creating; omit when republishing to keep the current icon.

shared_live.description: States who the artifact you are republishing is already shared with, and changes nothing: its 'read' value from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result. Required when that value is 'users' (named people or groups), 'org' (the user's whole organization) or 'public' (anyone with the link). Leave it out for a new artifact and when the value is 'owner'. Rejected if it does not match the artifact's current value.

slug.description: The artifact's server-assigned slug (UUID), e.g. from list_artifacts, get_artifact or the artifact's own URL. Omit to create a new artifact.

title.description: Browser-tab title. Required when creating. When republishing it is optional — omitted, the new version keeps the current live version's title (the server also keeps the stored HTML's <title> element in sync with it); pass a value only to rename the artifact, never invent a new title on a routine republish.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__read_artifact
tools.description: Read the current document of an artifact: one that the user owns, or one that belongs to someone in the user's organization and that the user can open. Read a pasted claude.ai artifact link with this tool. Returns a JSON summary (slug, version id, title, favicon, runtime-contract version, total_lines, and for a multi-file artifact its file names), then the HTML of the version the user is served, then a reminder. The HTML, and the summary's title, favicon and file names, are wrapped in an <untrusted-document-...> tag that the summary's notice names; the tag is not part of them. A document over ~1 MiB is not served whole: read it in parts with offset and limit, which count lines; next_offset says where the next part starts. ## Rule 1: Cost Confirmation
Before calling ANY tool that costs credits, ask which ai_model to use where there is a choice (prefer an explicit one), present the cost and wait for user confirmation.

| Tool | Credits |
|------|---------|

| meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d | table below |
| meshy_text_to_3d_refine / meshy_retexture | 10 (15 with texture_resolution "8k") |
| meshy_remesh / meshy_rig (incl. walking + running) / meshy_uv_unwrap | 5 |
| meshy_animate | 3 per action |
| meshy_text_to_motion | 10 (prime) / 3 (swift) |
| meshy_repair_printability / meshy_process_multicolor / meshy_auto_split | 10 |
| meshy_convert / meshy_resize | 1 |
| meshy_creative_lab | 36; keycap 62; fidget-collapsible 6 |

| analyze printability, balance, usage, animation library, status, list, download | free |

| image / multi-image ai_model | mesh only | + 2K/4K texture | + 8K texture |
|---|---|---|---|

If a create call fails with a timeout, network error or 5xx, the task may still have been created and charged. Check meshy_list_tasks (task_type = that task's type) for it before calling the create tool again. A wait that times out leaves the task running: poll the same task_id again.

target_formats is fixed at creation time (3mf only when listed), so ask about the intended use first.

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.
- The normal local flow attaches to the running Chrome/Chromium CDP endpoint. No browser ids or local profile selection.

## plugin:desktop-commander:desktop-commander
Desktop Commander provides tools for working with the user's authorized device.
- Filesystem tools handle direct file and directory operations within configured access boundaries.
- Terminal process tools support shell commands, REPLs, and long-running processes. start_process creates a process session; interact_with_process sends input; read_process_output reads later output; force_terminate ends a session.
- Search tools are session-based. start_search creates a search session; get_more_search_results reads its results; stop_search ends it early.
- Absolute paths are generally the most reliable because relative paths depend on the active working directory.
- allowedDirectories and each tool's schema, annotations, and documented constraints define the operational boundaries.

## claude-artifacts
Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL. When a finished piece of work is meant for other people or agents, such as a report for a team or the case for a decision the team has yet to make, Claude does not treat it as finished while it exists only in this conversation or in a local file. Claude publishes it and gives the person the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose. Claude publishes it even when the request is phrased as a question, such as "can you write up the plan?". When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. 258	#### Group C. Honest motion
259	
260	**IW-11. Continuous change and the honest settle (closed form).**
261	*Rule.* Everything in this rule applies **only when `motion_mode` is HONEST**. (a) **Continuous change.** Honest samples of `displayed_pm` arrive when the Filter's honest memo is invalidated (an LS-20 quantum crossing, at most once per Graph step, `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6); while the Graph value sits inside one quantum there is no sample. **For MVP the honest needle's resolution is the LS-20 quantum** (checkpoint ruling C14): each instrument keeps one presentation-local scalar `prev_honest_pm` (the scalar that extends the triple of (c), beside the native-unit `prev_honest_native` that D.3 formats the card numeral from *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*); a new honest sample is drawn as a ramp from `prev_honest_pm` to the new accepted `target_pm` (the sample after the reversal dwell of (b); equal to `displayed_pm` unless a one-quantum reversal is still held) over one Graph step (100 ms) through the single PR-8 rule-5 interpolator (`tick_alpha`), with no overshoot and no extrapolation, and the needle then rests. The drawn value therefore lags the true value by at most one Graph step plus the quantum, except for a genuine one-quantum reversal, which the reversal dwell of (b) holds for `INSTR_REVERSAL_DWELL_STEPS` more steps (at most 500 ms in all) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; the consequence channel tolerates both (AAV-17 requires direction agreement, not phase). A slow honest ramp reads as a mechanical detent (step, then rest), which strengthens "honest rests, the lie never rests"; a fast ramp (a decompression) crosses a quantum every step and reads as continuous. The quanta in needle terms (D.1, D.4): `p_o2` 5 dkPa over a 300 dkPa span is 16.7 pm, 1.7 px on DIAL_L and 1.25 px on DIAL_S; `P` 10 dkPa over 1100 is 9.1 pm; `T` 1000 mC over 150000 is 6.7 pm; `stock` 20 pm is 1 px at `travel_px` 50. `INSTR_SETTLE_JUMP_PM` 40 exceeds every single-quantum step (the largest is `p_o2`, 16.7 pm), so one quantum crossing never fires a settle on any quantity; on the one `settle_eligible` quantity, `load` (quantum `LOAD_QUANTUM_PERMILLE` 20 permille = 16.0 pm, D.1), three quanta accumulated inside the jump window (3 x 16 = 48 pm, over the 40 pm threshold; two = 32 pm, under it) do, see (b); the same three `p_o2` quanta (17 + 17 + 16 = 50 pm) are drawn by the D.1 ramp, because `settle_eligible` is false for `p_o2` (D.4). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G4: conforms to the per-quantity `settle_eligible` gate of D.4)* (b) **Rest, jump and settle: rest is defined in time.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier text defined rest per Graph step here and per sample in D.4 and AC-IW-17, a definition under which the settle could never fire on `p_o2` or `stock`.)* An instrument is **at rest** iff no honest sample has arrived for `INSTR_REST_STEPS` consecutive Graph steps (3 steps = 300 ms) and no settle is active; IW-11, D.4, E-IW-8, AC-IW-17 and the REST state of S2 all use this one definition. The first honest sample after rest opens a **jump window** of `INSTR_SETTLE_WINDOW_STEPS` Graph steps (4 steps = 400 ms) and records `rest_pm`, the value the needle held at rest. A *jump*, on a `settle_eligible` quantity only (D.4; `load` at MVP) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, is any sample inside that window with |`target_pm` - `rest_pm`| >= `INSTR_SETTLE_JUMP_PM` (the honest change accumulated since leaving rest, not the change of one step): a valve flick, a repair, an `apply_damage`, a breaker closing. The jump converts the in-flight ramp into a settle: the drawn value is the closed-form underdamped step response of D.4 as a pure function of `(from_pm, to_pm, t_jump)` and `present_time`, overshoot at most 5 % of the jump, settling to rest within 250-400 ms, then exactly still. A run that does not reach the threshold inside its window is a **sweep** (a continuing decompression crossing a quantum every step): it never settles until rest is re-entered, so a sustained ramp does not stutter. **The honest signature is therefore "step, then rest"**: every honest change is a detent-like step that ends at rest, and a real jump of at least 40 pm is a heavier damped ease; the overshoot shows as a 1-px tip flip only for jumps of 216 pm (DIAL_L) or 288 pm (DIAL_S) or more (D.4), and on the verified manifest actions only the `load` dial settles (D.4 reachability table). **Reversal dwell.** The LS-20 buckets have no hysteresis, so an honest value hovering on a quantum edge would flip the needle 1-2 px at up to 10 Hz with no stress descriptor, which reads as a tremor on a calm reading and teaches the lesson backwards. A sample that reverses the direction of the last accepted change by no more than one quantum is held as a candidate and accepted only after it has been the current sample for `INSTR_REVERSAL_DWELL_STEPS` Graph steps (4 = 400 ms); a candidate that equals the held value, or is superseded, is dropped. The needle, the card and the card numeral all use the accepted `target_pm`, so a 10 Hz dither across a quantum edge produces at most one move (AC-IW-110). (c) **State.** Exactly one `(from_pm, to_pm, t_jump)` triple per instrument plus the presentation-local scalars `prev_honest_pm` of (a) and `rest_pm`, the window start step and the dwell candidate (`target_pm`, `candidate_pm`, `t_candidate`) of (b), the triple discarded after `INSTR_SETTLE_MS`, neither ever persisted, never replicated, never read by any other *system*; the instrument's wall node and its card are two views of one instrument object and both draw from its single drawn value, which is what makes card parity (IW-26) hold. The triple, `prev_honest_pm` and the scalars of (b) are cleared by any non-HONEST frame and snapped by `hard_start` (the Filter's term, PF-33, raised by a kernel restore or `force_stage`), restore, camera cut and cull (IW-5, IW-33). The HUD's suit-arc settle (HS-14, `HUD_SETTLE_MS` 300 `[PH]`, HUD-owned; renamed there from `SETTLE_MS` after the collision, CF-HS-20) is a peer: it may cite `settle_response` (D.4) instead of restating a second curve, and this GDD's constants carry the `INSTR_` prefix so the two names never collide. (d) **Re-basing (orchestrator ruling: the ui-programmer's re-base adopted over the ux-designer's per-frame retarget, which would make the drawn value jump).** While a settle is active, any further change of the honest displayed value re-bases the triple: `from_pm` := the value currently drawn, `to_pm` := the new displayed value, `t_jump` := now; velocity is discarded (a small kink, accepted). So one triple always suffices, nothing accumulates, and a continuous ramp steeper than `INSTR_SETTLE_JUMP_PM` per step degrades into a first-order-like follower whose overshoot of each tiny delta is sub-pixel (no rubbery bounce). (e) Any `motion_mode` other than HONEST clears the triple at once and bypasses settle entirely: a lie never borrows settle (PF-17). Reduced motion: settle becomes a step (IW-27). (advisor ruling R10; K-2)
262	*Why.* ART 7.3 mandates a damped settle ("the ship changed; the instrument caught up"). PR-8's rationale (PIPE:198) rejected "a gauge's needle lag" as presentation-owned state because it threatened the truth channel; a gauge is module-body, not truth channel, and the closed form is a pure function of three scalars derived from values the player was already shown, with PF-11's "modulo presentation-local state" as precedent. This is the one bounded exemption from PR-8's rationale and is **carried as K-2 for the PIPE owner to acknowledge**, not silently overridden. The continuous path uses the one PR-8 rule-5 interpolator, so rule 5 itself is not violated.
263	*Edge notes.* **CONFLICT K-17 (resolved by checkpoint ruling C14; the Filter and Graph refreshes are routed).** PF-7 memoises an honest ref "per sanity run and invalidated by the notification that dirtied it", the honest `Perceived` carries no previous value, PF UI Requirements forbid caching a `Perceived`, and LS-20 fires dirty keys only on quantum crossings (`p_o2` 5 dkPa, `P` 10 dkPa, `T` 1000 mC, store 20 permille). So even a Filter-supplied previous value could buy at best a one-step ramp between quanta, and the honest needle's resolution is the LS-20 quantum (rule (a)). **Refresh landed in the Filter (PF UI Requirements, 2026-10-27; OQ-IW-1 closed)**: the no-cache sentence now reads "never cache a `Perceived` record; a presentation-local scalar derived from an honest displayed value and cleared on any non-HONEST frame, cull, cut and restore is not a cache". The earlier request for a Filter-supplied `displayed_prev_pm` is withdrawn. Option (B), the Filter refreshing the honest memo every Graph step for refs that have an on-screen instrument (about 18 refs at 10 Hz), would give a smooth ramp at a per-step cost and is carried as OQ-IW-18, not MVP. LSG:998 ("gauges read `read_view` at render rate for smooth needles") is still routed to the Graph as a refresh (R18 wins). A lie onset during an active settle clears the triple and the drawn needle snaps to `displayed_pm` by at most the settle's current deviation (the lie already shows its gleam floor and sound from its first frame, PF-15; the first lie is on a fault-free subject at rest, SN-16); letting the tail decay as an additive offset is **not** adopted (it brushes R8 and PF-17; OQ-IW-6). When the mode returns to HONEST (CLEAR, PF-12) no jump is detected because the displayed value tracked the true value during the return; a RETURN is a glide to truth, not a jump.
264	
265	**IW-12. Honest tremor: driven only by physical stress, only when HONEST.**
266	*Rule.* A DIAL or LINEAR instrument whose `motion_mode` is HONEST **and** whose stress predicate holds draws tremor: an irregular positional offset of at most `TREMOR_AMP_PX` (+-1 art px, ART 7.3), at 6-10 Hz, around the displayed value, with no gleam, onset ramp `TREMOR_ONSET_MS`, ceasing with decay `TREMOR_DECAY_MS` when the predicate ends, and resting on a pixel. At zoom rung `k` 1 the amplitude is raised to keep at least `TREMOR_MIN_SCREEN_PX` (2) screen px (D.5; a refinement of ART 7.3's +-1, OQ-IW-4). The **stress predicate** (MVP) is any of: (i) an active hazard-mode FailureDescriptor on the bound node, mode in {1 LEAK, 2 SHORT, 3 OVERHEAT, 4 FREEZE, 5 BREACH, 7 OVERLOAD} (LS-11), with `sev` >= `TREMOR_SEV_MIN` (1), read through `failures(filter)`; never mode 10 WORN, 6 STARVE, 8 SEVERED, 9 SCRAM or **27 PATCH_WEEP** (a patched subject's steady weep, LS-11 row 27: `hp_cap < HP_FULL` with no mode 1-9 live, no `intensity_pm`; it is a consequence-channel witness of the patch, not a stress) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, and never a compartment band descriptor (ATMO_COLD / HOT / THIN / DECOMP 20-23, AIRFLOW 24, PUDDLE 25): a band is a state, not a stress (advisor final-review amendment to R9: `warn_elapsed` is > 0 for every sev-1 subject, LSG D.11, so it is not a tremor input); (ii) an active OVERLOAD (mode 7) descriptor on a CABLE of the bound loop component, through `failures(filter)` (LSG:127); (iii) an active `SEAL_STRAIN` descriptor on an OPENING of the bound compartment, or a `LEAK` or `BREACH` descriptor on a HULL_SEGMENT or SEAM bounding it (subjects found through `nodes_in(cid)` and `neighbors(cid)`; read through `failures(filter)`); the subject lists of (i)-(iii) are precomputed at section load and recomputed only on a topology dirty key (`T`, `SEC/<id>`), never per frame. (iv) **`stress_active(section_id)`, off by default** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the MVP predicate is (i)-(iii) only, and (iv) is read only if the knob `TREMOR_USE_SECTION_STRESS` is true (default **false**, registered in Tuning Knobs); (K-13 resolved: the Graph now publishes the pure query, LS-19 additions, 2026-10-27; section stress is `stress_pm` = `BREACH_PROPAGATION_MULT` 2000 while `step_no < stress_until_step`, set by M17 STRESS for `STRESS_HOLD_STEPS` 600) for an instrument in that section. **(iv) is provisional and off:** M17 STRESS has one caller, Attention, which this rule forbids as a tremor driver (a tremor driven by it would make an instrument show Attention, which the header and IW-28 forbid, AT-17), and AT C1 reads a needle moved by real STRESS damage as a consequence and not a tell; the creative-director's position is that (iv) as written is a pillar-level conflict, so it stays off until the Attention owner and the creative-director confirm the contrary reading (OQ-IW-38); with the knob false the predicate is (i)-(iii) and `stress_active` is not read by Instruments. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The predicate is refreshed once per Graph step (IW-5). Tremor is never driven by Attention, sanity, a timer or a lie. It is positional, not luminous (HR-13 exemption; shown on the card as well, suppressed under `reduced_motion`, D96) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. It is evaluated only when `motion_mode` is HONEST (advisor ruling R9; AT-17, AT:1415 C1).
267	**On the card (Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20): D96 — the card shows the honest tremor, suppressed under `reduced_motion`; K-18 resolved) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.** The card shows the same honest tremor as its wall gauge (parity, IW-26; the amplitude is +-`TREMOR_AMP_PX` HUD art px, never scaled by the card multiple). With `reduced_motion` on, the tremor is suppressed on the card exactly as on the wall gauge and the held stress notch pair of IW-27 and D.10 shows in its place (two Hull Grey squares on the Ground plate above the dial) while the predicate holds and the reading is HONEST, so the stress tell never depends on motion for a player who has asked for less of it. The earlier objection (HR-13 says "no HUD shake"; ART:984 flags tremor's positional-not-luminous status as unconfirmed) is answered by this suppression and by the card frame, plate and keycaps never moving; the former fallback (the held notch on the card in all modes) is retired unless the user declines this default. Further accessibility-specialist advice is welcome when Accessibility Settings is designed, but nothing here waits on it.
268	*Why.* P2: the honest tremor is the instrument's share of the 10-30 s tell and is a real consequence the player can trace. "A needle moved by STRESS damage is a consequence, not a tell Attention drives" (AT C1). Because a tremor exists only on an honest reading, "shake = real" is a rule the game never breaks.
269	*Edge notes.* A patched or WORN subject carries only mode 10 WORN (LS-11, LS-23), so it does not tremble; its `warn_elapsed` is > 0 (LSG D.11), which is why `warn_elapsed` is not a tremor input. `alarm_eligible` (`sev` >= 3, LS-13) is not a tremor input; tremor begins at the first physical stress, always before the alarm class (`W_MIN_WARNING_S` 10 is the Graph's). If the predicate flaps at Graph-step rate, tremor flaps with it (10 Hz worst case); `TREMOR_HOLD_S` (default 0) is the playtest remedy. Tremor's perceptibility at `k` 1 on the largest field is marginal (D.7); the design accepts it, since the tell is for a player standing at the instrument. **Instrument tremor is never the only tell (stage-12 CD-GDD-ALIGN concern 6).** It is this system's share of the P2 10-30 s tell and P2 is carried by several channels: every stress source in predicates (i)-(iii) above must also have a sound tell or a world-witness tell owned by Adaptive Audio or Failure & Trail (strain creak, hiss, drip, spark or frost, per the consequence channel), so zooming out to `k` 1, or standing outside the light, never removes the warning. This is a cross-owner requirement checked by AC-IW-106 and routed to Adaptive Audio and Failure & Trail.
270

272	*Rule.* The Filter's `motion_mode` is the only switch:
273

282	An honest gauge never glides; a lie never settles or trembles; the instrument never infers a lie, it only obeys the mode. (PF-7 edge note, PF-17; orchestrator ruling R8 of the Filter run)

284	*Edge notes.* The card has the identical dispatch (IW-26). **TICK and STALE are modes of the card numeral only** (checkpoint ruling C2): a wall gauge carries no digit (IW-6), and a `lie_displayed_value` lie moves a FALSE_OK or FALSE_FAIL needle toward its zone and never holds it. The numeral's STALE hold is a card-visible mode of the same lie, not a second one; the gleam and the motion mode remain mandatory and only the sound is droppable (PF-8).
285	
286	**IW-14. The numeral: honest ticking, the throttle, and who owns the scheduler.**
287	*Rule.* Numerals exist only on the card (IW-6). An honest numeral steps once per real change of `displayed_value` at the quantity's `lsb`, never tweens and never counts up; a transition is a digit-glyph substitution in tabular cells (fixed width, slashed zero) of only the cells whose glyph changed, and never inverts a plate (PF-18; HR-13 is then checkable per cell). The card's honest numeral changes only on the HUD's shared `HONEST_TICK_MS` grid boundary and adds no luminance event of its own (HS-47); a boundary at which no card digit changes is not an event; when the HUD's grid-skip rule skips a boundary the card shows the then-latest step at the next one, so honest numeral lag is at most `2 x HONEST_TICK_MS`. # Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.
