258	#### Group C. Honest motion
259	
260	**IW-11. Continuous change and the honest settle (closed form).**
261	*Rule.* Everything in this rule applies **only when `motion_mode` is HONEST**. (a) **Continuous change.** Honest samples of `displayed_pm` arrive when the Filter's honest memo is invalidated (an LS-20 quantum crossing, at most once per Graph step, `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6); while the Graph value sits inside one quantum there is no sample. **For MVP the honest needle's resolution is the LS-20 quantum** (checkpoint ruling C14): each instrument keeps one presentation-local scalar `prev_honest_pm` (the scalar that extends the triple of (c), beside the native-unit `prev_honest_native` that D.3 formats the card numeral from *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*); a new honest sample is drawn as a ramp from `prev_honest_pm` to the new accepted `target_pm` (the sample after the reversal dwell of (b); equal to `displayed_pm` unless a one-quantum reversal is still held) over one Graph step (100 ms) through the single PR-8 rule-5 interpolator (`tick_alpha`), with no overshoot and no extrapolation, and the needle then rests. The drawn value therefore lags the true value by at most one Graph step plus the quantum, except for a genuine one-quantum reversal, which the reversal dwell of (b) holds for `INSTR_REVERSAL_DWELL_STEPS` more steps (at most 500 ms in all) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; the consequence channel tolerates both (AAV-17 requires direction agreement, not phase). A slow honest ramp reads as a mechanical detent (step, then rest), which strengthens "honest rests, the lie never rests"; a fast ramp (a decompression) crosses a quantum every step and reads as continuous. The quanta in needle terms (D.1, D.4): `p_o2` 5 dkPa over a 300 dkPa span is 16.7 pm, 1.7 px on DIAL_L and 1.25 px on DIAL_S; `P` 10 dkPa over 1100 is 9.1 pm; `T` 1000 mC over 150000 is 6.7 pm; `stock` 20 pm is 1 px at `travel_px` 50. `INSTR_SETTLE_JUMP_PM` 40 exceeds every single-quantum step (the largest is `p_o2`, 16.7 pm), so one quantum crossing never fires a settle on any quantity; on the one `settle_eligible` quantity, `load` (quantum `LOAD_QUANTUM_PERMILLE` 20 permille = 16.0 pm, D.1), three quanta accumulated inside the jump window (3 x 16 = 48 pm, over the 40 pm threshold; two = 32 pm, under it) do, see (b); the same three `p_o2` quanta (17 + 17 + 16 = 50 pm) are drawn by the D.1 ramp, because `settle_eligible` is false for `p_o2` (D.4). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling G4: conforms to the per-quantity `settle_eligible` gate of D.4)* (b) **Rest, jump and settle: rest is defined in time.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier text defined rest per Graph step here and per sample in D.4 and AC-IW-17, a definition under which the settle could never fire on `p_o2` or `stock`.)* An instrument is **at rest** iff no honest sample has arrived for `INSTR_REST_STEPS` consecutive Graph steps (3 steps = 300 ms) and no settle is active; IW-11, D.4, E-IW-8, AC-IW-17 and the REST state of S2 all use this one definition. The first honest sample after rest opens a **jump window** of `INSTR_SETTLE_WINDOW_STEPS` Graph steps (4 steps = 400 ms) and records `rest_pm`, the value the needle held at rest. A *jump*, on a `settle_eligible` quantity only (D.4; `load` at MVP) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, is any sample inside that window with |`target_pm` - `rest_pm`| >= `INSTR_SETTLE_JUMP_PM` (the honest change accumulated since leaving rest, not the change of one step): a valve flick, a repair, an `apply_damage`, a breaker closing. The jump converts the in-flight ramp into a settle: the drawn value is the closed-form underdamped step response of D.4 as a pure function of `(from_pm, to_pm, t_jump)` and `present_time`, overshoot at most 5 % of the jump, settling to rest within 250-400 ms, then exactly still. A run that does not reach the threshold inside its window is a **sweep** (a continuing decompression crossing a quantum every step): it never settles until rest is re-entered, so a sustained ramp does not stutter. **The honest signature is therefore "step, then rest"**: every honest change is a detent-like step that ends at rest, and a real jump of at least 40 pm is a heavier damped ease; the overshoot shows as a 1-px tip flip only for jumps of 216 pm (DIAL_L) or 288 pm (DIAL_S) or more (D.4), and on the verified manifest actions only the `load` dial settles (D.4 reachability table). **Reversal dwell.** The LS-20 buckets have no hysteresis, so an honest value hovering on a quantum edge would flip the needle 1-2 px at up to 10 Hz with no stress descriptor, which reads as a tremor on a calm reading and teaches the lesson backwards. A sample that reverses the direction of the last accepted change by no more than one quantum is held as a candidate and accepted only after it has been the current sample for `INSTR_REVERSAL_DWELL_STEPS` Graph steps (4 = 400 ms); a candidate that equals the held value, or is superseded, is dropped. The needle, the card and the card numeral all use the accepted `target_pm`, so a 10 Hz dither across a quantum edge produces at most one move (AC-IW-110). (c) **State.** Exactly one `(from_pm, to_pm, t_jump)` triple per instrument plus the presentation-local scalars `prev_honest_pm` of (a) and `rest_pm`, the window start step and the dwell candidate (`target_pm`, `candidate_pm`, `t_candidate`) of (b), the triple discarded after `INSTR_SETTLE_MS`, neither ever persisted, never replicated, never read by any other *system*; the instrument's wall node and its card are two views of one instrument object and both draw from its single drawn value, which is what makes card parity (IW-26) hold. The triple, `prev_honest_pm` and the scalars of (b) are cleared by any non-HONEST frame and snapped by `hard_start` (the Filter's term, PF-33, raised by a kernel restore or `force_stage`), restore, camera cut and cull (IW-5, IW-33). The HUD's suit-arc settle (HS-14, `HUD_SETTLE_MS` 300 `[PH]`, HUD-owned; renamed there from `SETTLE_MS` after the collision, CF-HS-20) is a peer: it may cite `settle_response` (D.4) instead of restating a second curve, and this GDD's constants carry the `INSTR_` prefix so the two names never collide. (d) **Re-basing (orchestrator ruling: the ui-programmer's re-base adopted over the ux-designer's per-frame retarget, which would make the drawn value jump).** While a settle is active, any further change of the honest displayed value re-bases the triple: `from_pm` := the value currently drawn, `to_pm` := the new displayed value, `t_jump` := now; velocity is discarded (a small kink, accepted). So one triple always suffices, nothing accumulates, and a continuous ramp steeper than `INSTR_SETTLE_JUMP_PM` per step degrades into a first-order-like follower whose overshoot of each tiny delta is sub-pixel (no rubbery bounce). (e) Any `motion_mode` other than HONEST clears the triple at once and bypasses settle entirely: a lie never borrows settle (PF-17). Reduced motion: settle becomes a step (IW-27). (advisor ruling R10; K-2)
262	*Why.* ART 7.3 mandates a damped settle ("the ship changed; the instrument caught up"). PR-8's rationale (PIPE:198) rejected "a gauge's needle lag" as presentation-owned state because it threatened the truth channel; a gauge is module-body, not truth channel, and the closed form is a pure function of three scalars derived from values the player was already shown, with PF-11's "modulo presentation-local state" as precedent. This is the one bounded exemption from PR-8's rationale and is **carried as K-2 for the PIPE owner to acknowledge**, not silently overridden. The continuous path uses the one PR-8 rule-5 interpolator, so rule 5 itself is not violated.
263	*Edge notes.* **CONFLICT K-17 (resolved by checkpoint ruling C14; the Filter and Graph refreshes are routed).** PF-7 memoises an honest ref "per sanity run and invalidated by the notification that dirtied it", the honest `Perceived` carries no previous value, PF UI Requirements forbid caching a `Perceived`, and LS-20 fires dirty keys only on quantum crossings (`p_o2` 5 dkPa, `P` 10 dkPa, `T` 1000 mC, store 20 permille). So even a Filter-supplied previous value could buy at best a one-step ramp between quanta, and the honest needle's resolution is the LS-20 quantum (rule (a)). **Refresh landed in the Filter (PF UI Requirements, 2026-10-27; OQ-IW-1 closed)**: the no-cache sentence now reads "never cache a `Perceived` record; a presentation-local scalar derived from an honest displayed value and cleared on any non-HONEST frame, cull, cut and restore is not a cache". The earlier request for a Filter-supplied `displayed_prev_pm` is withdrawn. Option (B), the Filter refreshing the honest memo every Graph step for refs that have an on-screen instrument (about 18 refs at 10 Hz), would give a smooth ramp at a per-step cost and is carried as OQ-IW-18, not MVP. LSG:998 ("gauges read `read_view` at render rate for smooth needles") is still routed to the Graph as a refresh (R18 wins). A lie onset during an active settle clears the triple and the drawn needle snaps to `displayed_pm` by at most the settle's current deviation (the lie already shows its gleam floor and sound from its first frame, PF-15; the first lie is on a fault-free subject at rest, SN-16); letting the tail decay as an additive offset is **not** adopted (it brushes R8 and PF-17; OQ-IW-6). When the mode returns to HONEST (CLEAR, PF-12) no jump is detected because the displayed value tracked the true value during the return; a RETURN is a glide to truth, not a jump.
264	
265	**IW-12. Honest tremor: driven only by physical stress, only when HONEST.**
266	*Rule.* A DIAL or LINEAR instrument whose `motion_mode` is HONEST **and** whose stress predicate holds draws tremor: an irregular positional offset of at most `TREMOR_AMP_PX` (+-1 art px, ART 7.3), at 6-10 Hz, around the displayed value, with no gleam, onset ramp `TREMOR_ONSET_MS`, ceasing with decay `TREMOR_DECAY_MS` when the predicate ends, and resting on a pixel. At zoom rung `k` 1 the amplitude is raised to keep at least `TREMOR_MIN_SCREEN_PX` (2) screen px (D.5; a refinement of ART 7.3's +-1, OQ-IW-4). The **stress predicate** (MVP) is any of: (i) an active hazard-mode FailureDescriptor on the bound node, mode in {1 LEAK, 2 SHORT, 3 OVERHEAT, 4 FREEZE, 5 BREACH, 7 OVERLOAD} (LS-11), with `sev` >= `TREMOR_SEV_MIN` (1), read through `failures(filter)`; never mode 10 WORN, 6 STARVE, 8 SEVERED, 9 SCRAM or **27 PATCH_WEEP** (a patched subject's steady weep, LS-11 row 27: `hp_cap < HP_FULL` with no mode 1-9 live, no `intensity_pm`; it is a consequence-channel witness of the patch, not a stress) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, and never a compartment band descriptor (ATMO_COLD / HOT / THIN / DECOMP 20-23, AIRFLOW 24, PUDDLE 25): a band is a state, not a stress (advisor final-review amendment to R9: `warn_elapsed` is > 0 for every sev-1 subject, LSG D.11, so it is not a tremor input); (ii) an active OVERLOAD (mode 7) descriptor on a CABLE of the bound loop component, through `failures(filter)` (LSG:127); (iii) an active `SEAL_STRAIN` descriptor on an OPENING of the bound compartment, or a `LEAK` or `BREACH` descriptor on a HULL_SEGMENT or SEAM bounding it (subjects found through `nodes_in(cid)` and `neighbors(cid)`; read through `failures(filter)`); the subject lists of (i)-(iii) are precomputed at section load and recomputed only on a topology dirty key (`T`, `SEC/<id>`), never per frame. (iv) **`stress_active(section_id)`, off by default** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the MVP predicate is (i)-(iii) only, and (iv) is read only if the knob `TREMOR_USE_SECTION_STRESS` is true (default **false**, registered in Tuning Knobs); (K-13 resolved: the Graph now publishes the pure query, LS-19 additions, 2026-10-27; section stress is `stress_pm` = `BREACH_PROPAGATION_MULT` 2000 while `step_no < stress_until_step`, set by M17 STRESS for `STRESS_HOLD_STEPS` 600) for an instrument in that section. **(iv) is provisional and off:** M17 STRESS has one caller, Attention, which this rule forbids as a tremor driver (a tremor driven by it would make an instrument show Attention, which the header and IW-28 forbid, AT-17), and AT C1 reads a needle moved by real STRESS damage as a consequence and not a tell; the creative-director's position is that (iv) as written is a pillar-level conflict, so it stays off until the Attention owner and the creative-director confirm the contrary reading (OQ-IW-38); with the knob false the predicate is (i)-(iii) and `stress_active` is not read by Instruments. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The predicate is refreshed once per Graph step (IW-5). Tremor is never driven by Attention, sanity, a timer or a lie. It is positional, not luminous (HR-13 exemption; shown on the card as well, suppressed under `reduced_motion`, D96) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. It is evaluated only when `motion_mode` is HONEST (advisor ruling R9; AT-17, AT:1415 C1).
267	**On the card (Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20): D96 — the card shows the honest tremor, suppressed under `reduced_motion`; K-18 resolved) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.** The card shows the same honest tremor as its wall gauge (parity, IW-26; the amplitude is +-`TREMOR_AMP_PX` HUD art px, never scaled by the card multiple). With `reduced_motion` on, the tremor is suppressed on the card exactly as on the wall gauge and the held stress notch pair of IW-27 and D.10 shows in its place (two Hull Grey squares on the Ground plate above the dial) while the predicate holds and the reading is HONEST, so the stress tell never depends on motion for a player who has asked for less of it. The earlier objection (HR-13 says "no HUD shake"; ART:984 flags tremor's positional-not-luminous status as unconfirmed) is answered by this suppression and by the card frame, plate and keycaps never moving; the former fallback (the held notch on the card in all modes) is retired unless the user declines this default. Further accessibility-specialist advice is welcome when Accessibility Settings is designed, but nothing here waits on it.
268	*Why.* P2: the honest tremor is the instrument's share of the 10-30 s tell and is a real consequence the player can trace. "A needle moved by STRESS damage is a consequence, not a tell Attention drives" (AT C1). Because a tremor exists only on an honest reading, "shake = real" is a rule the game never breaks.
269	*Edge notes.* A patched or WORN subject carries only mode 10 WORN (LS-11, LS-23), so it does not tremble; its `warn_elapsed` is > 0 (LSG D.11), which is why `warn_elapsed` is not a tremor input. `alarm_eligible` (`sev` >= 3, LS-13) is not a tremor input; tremor begins at the first physical stress, always before the alarm class (`W_MIN_WARNING_S` 10 is the Graph's). If the predicate flaps at Graph-step rate, tremor flaps with it (10 Hz worst case); `TREMOR_HOLD_S` (default 0) is the playtest remedy. Tremor's perceptibility at `k` 1 on the largest field is marginal (D.7); the design accepts it, since the tell is for a player standing at the instrument. **Instrument tremor is never the only tell (stage-12 CD-GDD-ALIGN concern 6).** It is this system's share of the P2 10-30 s tell and P2 is carried by several channels: every stress source in predicates (i)-(iii) above must also have a sound tell or a world-witness tell owned by Adaptive Audio or Failure & Trail (strain creak, hiss, drip, spark or frost, per the consequence channel), so zooming out to `k` 1, or standing outside the light, never removes the warning. This is a cross-owner requirement checked by AC-IW-106 and routed to Adaptive Audio and Failure & Trail.
270	
271	**IW-13. Motion-mode dispatch.**
272	*Rule.* The Filter's `motion_mode` is the only switch:
273	
274	| `motion_mode` | Needle / meniscus | Numeral (card) | Settle | Tremor | Stress notch (RM) | Drawn value from |
275	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
276	| HONEST | `displayed_pm` through IW-11 and IW-12 | steps once per real change (throttled, IW-14) | yes | yes if predicate | yes if predicate | Instruments |
277	| GLIDE | `displayed_pm` verbatim (the Filter's trajectory, wander included) | continuous tick follows | no | no | no | the Filter's value; Instruments draw it |
278	| TICK | `displayed_pm` verbatim (the Filter's trajectory, wander included) | continuous tick, `T_tick` (PF-18) | no | no | no | same |
279	| STALE | `displayed_pm` verbatim (the Filter's trajectory, wander included) | held digits | no | no | no | same |
280	| RETURN | `displayed_pm` verbatim (the Filter's trajectory: the rate-limited follower to truth) | follows | no | no | no | same |
281	
282	An honest gauge never glides; a lie never settles or trembles; the instrument never infers a lie, it only obeys the mode. (PF-7 edge note, PF-17; orchestrator ruling R8 of the Filter run)
283	*Why.* If Instruments could decide, the player could read the truth from which animation applies: a P4 oracle.
284	*Edge notes.* The card has the identical dispatch (IW-26). **TICK and STALE are modes of the card numeral only** (checkpoint ruling C2): a wall gauge carries no digit (IW-6), and a `lie_displayed_value` lie moves a FALSE_OK or FALSE_FAIL needle toward its zone and never holds it. No lying needle rests: whatever the numeral's mode, the needle draws the Filter's trajectory, which never rests (PF-17), so the wall gauge keeps its motion mode while the card is closed (PF-8, HR-5). The numeral's STALE hold is a card-visible mode of the same lie, not a second one; the gleam and the motion mode remain mandatory and only the sound is droppable (PF-8).
285	
286	**IW-14. The numeral: honest ticking, the throttle, and who owns the scheduler.**
287	*Rule.* Numerals exist only on the card (IW-6). An honest numeral steps once per real change of `displayed_value` at the quantity's `lsb`, never tweens and never counts up; a transition is a digit-glyph substitution in tabular cells (fixed width, slashed zero) of only the cells whose glyph changed, and never inverts a plate (PF-18; HR-13 is then checkable per cell). Honest transitions are throttled to the same ceiling as lying ones: the card's numeral updates on the HUD's shared **hold grid** `HONEST_TICK_MS` (owner HUD & Suit Layer, HS-14, pinned 500 ms and ratified 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions, D91 iii) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; the 400-500 range is withdrawn, the HUD's window-feasibility check leaves 30 ticks as the only feasible grid, HS-47; PF-18's 334 is the bound without the beacon share and is not used here), at most `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` 3 transitions per rolling second; no second constant is registered here. At each grid boundary the numeral shows the **then-current** step (it may skip steps, never queued, never faded; it never shows a value the room did not have). The card's honest numeral changes only on the HUD's shared `HONEST_TICK_MS` grid boundary and adds no luminance event of its own (HS-47); a boundary at which no card digit changes is not an event; when the HUD's grid-skip rule skips a boundary the card shows the then-latest step at the next one, so honest numeral lag is at most `2 x HONEST_TICK_MS`. A lying numeral is the Filter's: a continuous tick or a stale hold under the shared scheduler `T_tick` = max(`LIE_TICK_MS` 400, N_r x 334) (400 / 668 / 1002 / 1336 ms for N_r 1..4; the 334 ms stagger floor keeps any closed 1 s window at or under `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` 3) (PF-18, registry `lying_digit_tick_schedule`); Instruments only draw the received digits. Formatting is integer-only: the displayed value is `displayed_value` converted by the quantity table (IW-9) with no float formatting; a temperature that rounds to -0 shows "0"; a value beyond the span shows the clamped bound with no "<" mark (a "<" would be a second reading); the format never reveals more precision than `lsb`. **`lsb` visibility lint:** for a lie-eligible dial, `lsb` must be fine enough that the digit changes at least every `T_VIS_MAX_S` during a glide at the floor rate (otherwise a lying numeral looks stale and the tri-modal rule loses a mode on the card): `p_o2` is therefore shown in kPa with one decimal (`lsb` 1 dkPa), not in whole kPa (D.12). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)*
288	*Why.* ART 7.3 (honest numerals tick); HR-13 (no luminance change faster than 3 Hz); PF-18.
289	*Edge notes.* **CONFLICT K-16 (raised by the ux-designer):** locked fact 21 / ART 7.3 say an honest numeral ticks "one step per real change, never a tween", while HR-13 and `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` 3 cap digit-glyph substitutions at 3 per second; a breach would exceed the cap if every step were shown. This GDD throttles and shows the then-current step, exactly as HUD & Suit Layer does for its own honest numerals (HS-14 amends the same locked rule, and its K8 row accepts the amendment); exempting honest ticks from the ceiling is rejected because a photosensitive player gains nothing from the distinction. Honest grid boundaries on the card are not counted in the Filter's `N_r` (which counts lying readouts only); the combined HUD budget (card numeral plus suit numerals plus lying readouts) is the HUD's arbiter HS-47, which itself records an open counting unit and an ASK to the Filter and the accessibility-specialist when lying digits at `N_r` 2 or more fill the ceiling *(OQ-IW-9: HS-47 states that the card's honest numeral shares the HUD's grid boundary and adds no event; the open counting unit is HUD CF-HS-10)*. The digit mechanism (glyph-cell substitution from a `ui_` atlas versus a text node) is -> ADR candidate; tabular numerals, slashed-zero shaping and integer-scale snapping of a vector font are `[UNV]` for the pinned build and ART 7.1 makes them asset-test requirements. The same honest-digit mechanism is offered as a reusable component to HUD & Suit Layer for the field-check reading (IW-35).
290	
291	**IW-15. Zone bands are coded by pattern first, hue second.**
292	*Rule.* Every dial and linear instrument carries zone bands derived **at build time** from LS-7 band names (D.2), never typed as numbers in instrument data. A band has a pattern class: SOLID (normal-class bands: `NORMAL`, `COMFORT`), HATCHED (caution: `THIN`, `LOW`, `COOL`, `HOT`, `FROST`), NOTCHED (critical: `HYPOXIC`, `ANOXIC`, `DECOMP`, `VACUUM`, `SCORCH`, `FREEZING`, `DEEP_COLD`; overload for `load`); the three must be distinguishable from each other at 25 % scale in greyscale (the hue-removed test). Gauge faces carry no loop hue (identity is the fitting silhouette and, while running, the pip); Alarm Red is never a zone colour (a static red band on every dial would make red common and decorative, violating ART 4.1). A zone narrower than `ZONE_MIN_ARC_PX` (6 art px of arc, D.2) fails a build lint: the instrument must use a larger size class or merge bands in data. The needle position is geometry; the needle is **not** coloured by the Graph's hysteretic `band_*` fields (advisor ruling R11).
293	*Why.* Hue-removed readability (ART 4.7, HR-5 test); LS-7 is the single source of bands.
294	*Edge notes.* Because LS-7 bands carry hysteresis (`H_P` 5 dkPa, `H_T` 500 mC) while dial zones are static intervals, the needle can sit inside the NORMAL zone while the Graph's `band_o2` still reads THIN: the dial is a continuous reading and no consumer compares them. The exact authored patterns (hatched dashes, split-rail, notched teeth) at a 3-row DIAL_S band are the pixel mock's to confirm (OQ-IW-3).
295	
296	#### Group D. Lying surfaces, state frames and the alarm mark

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

</system-reminder>

The tremor is STARTED and its predicate is read only when `motion_mode` is HONEST (advisor ruling R9; AT-17, AT:1415 C1). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: Perception Filter publishes `tremor_weight_pm` and BREATH, PF-8, PF-17)* **Onset of a lie: a running tremor fades, it does not stop.** Instruments read `tremor_weight_pm` (int 0..1000, the tenth `Perceived` field, PF-8; 1000 on every HONEST frame; read from the same single `perceived()` pull as `displayed_pm`, never computed or cached here). In the first non-HONEST frame the presenter latches `env_hold := env` of the last HONEST frame (0 if no tremor was running) and from then on (a) no new tremor starts and no onset ramp runs in any non-HONEST frame (the predicate is not read; a flag cannot be set in a non-HONEST frame), (b) env stays `env_hold` (no rise, no decay of its own; the fade is carried by `tremor_weight_pm` alone), (c) the drawn offset is the D.5 offset multiplied by `tremor_weight_pm / 1000`, which falls linearly from 1000 on the first ACTIVE frame to 0 over `TREMOR_BLEND_S` (Filter-owned, := `WANDER_ONSET_S`, 1.0 s `[PLACEHOLDER]`) and stays 0 until CLEAR, and (d) the flag clears and `env_hold` is discarded when `tremor_weight_pm` reaches 0, on `hard_start`, cull, camera cut and restore (so a restore mid-fade shows no tremor: Instruments never start one), and at the first HONEST frame after the lie (CLEAR): the predicate is then re-read and, if stress still holds, a fresh `TREMOR_ONSET_MS` ramp starts from env 0; `env_hold` is never carried across CLEAR. The **settle triple and the reduced-motion notch are the opposite: they are cleared at once** in the first non-HONEST frame (IW-11 (e), IW-27); under `reduced_motion` the tremor is not drawn, so there is nothing to fade and only the immediate notch clearing applies. In the first non-HONEST frame the presenter latches `env_hold := env` of the last HONEST frame (0 if no tremor was running) and from then on (a) no new tremor starts and no onset ramp runs in any non-HONEST frame (the predicate is not read; a flag cannot be set in a non-HONEST frame), (b) env stays `env_hold` (no rise, no decay of its own; the fade is carried by `tremor_weight_pm` alone), (c) the drawn offset is the D.5 offset multiplied by `tremor_weight_pm / 1000`, which falls linearly from 1000 on the first ACTIVE frame to 0 over `TREMOR_BLEND_S` (Filter-owned, := `WANDER_ONSET_S`, 1.0 s `[PLACEHOLDER]`) and stays 0 until CLEAR, and (d) the flag clears and `env_hold` is discarded when `tremor_weight_pm` reaches 0, on `hard_start`, cull, camera cut and restore (so a restore mid-fade shows no tremor: Instruments never start one), and at the first HONEST frame after the lie (CLEAR): the predicate is then re-read and, if stress still holds, a fresh `TREMOR_ONSET_MS` ramp starts from env 0; `env_hold` is never carried across CLEAR. The **settle triple and the reduced-motion notch are the opposite: they are cleared at once** in the first non-HONEST frame (IW-11 (e), IW-27); under `reduced_motion` the tremor is not drawn, so there is nothing to fade and only the immediate notch clearing applies. p='design/gdd/in-world-instruments-and-inspect-view.md'
s=open(p,encoding='utf-8').read()

old_end=s.index("*Why.* If Instruments could decide")
new="""*Rule.* The Filter's `motion_mode` (HONEST, GLIDE, TICK, STALE, BREATH, RETURN) is the only switch: *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)*

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HONEST | `displayed_pm` through IW-11 and IW-12 | steps once per real change (throttled, IW-14) | yes | yes if predicate (`tremor_weight_pm` 1000) | yes if predicate | Instruments |
| GLIDE | `displayed_pm` verbatim (the Filter's trajectory, wander included) | continuous tick follows | no | no new tremor; a tremor running at onset fades by `tremor_weight_pm` (D.5) | no (cleared that frame) | the Filter's value; Instruments draw it |
| TICK | `displayed_pm` verbatim (the Filter's trajectory, wander included) | continuous tick, `T_tick` (PF-18) | no | same as GLIDE | no | same |
| STALE | `displayed_pm` verbatim (the Filter's trajectory, wander included) | held digits | no | same as GLIDE | no | same |
| RETURN | `displayed_pm` verbatim (the Filter's trajectory: the rate-limited follower to truth) | follows | no | same as GLIDE (`tremor_weight_pm` is 0 once its blend is over and stays 0 until CLEAR) | no | same |
| BREATH *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: PF-8, PF-15 table, PF L335, L554)* | none: the surface is a static pair (state glyph, lamp-housing glow, machine state) with no needle; `frame_override` (the other honest frame of the pair, IW-17) is drawn and held still for the whole lie | none | no | no (a tremor exists only on a DIAL or LINEAR needle, IW-12, so none can be running; `tremor_weight_pm` is ignored) | no | `frame_override` from the Filter; the gleam breathes between `floor_eff` and `AMP_MAX_PM` over 4 to 6 s, drawn from `leak_amplitude_pm` exactly as IW-16 already draws any amplitude (no new behaviour) |

An honest gauge never glides; a lie never settles and never starts a tremor (a tremor already running at onset fades through `tremor_weight_pm`, IW-12, D.5); the instrument never infers a lie, it only obeys the mode. (PF-7 edge note, PF-17; orchestrator ruling R8 of the Filter run) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)*
"""
s=s[:old_start]+new+s[old_end:]
old="*Edge notes.* The card has the identical dispatch (IW-26)."
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old,"*Edge notes.* The card has the identical dispatch (IW-26). A numeral-only READOUT (`gauge_kind` READOUT, no needle) lying FALSE_OK or FALSE_FAIL arrives as STALE (not BREATH) with its gleam breathing through `leak_amplitude_pm` (PF L334, L789); BREATH is the record mode of static-pair refs only (`.glyph`, `.housing_glow`, `.machine_frame`). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)*",1)
open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s)
EOF
grep -n "BREATH" design/gdd/in-world-instruments-and-inspect-view.md | cut -c1-80

content.content:
484	#### S2. Motion axis (inside `DARK`, `LIT`, `CARD_OPEN`; independent of visibility)
485	
486	*(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* `REST`, `SETTLING` and `FILTER_DRIVEN` are mutually exclusive states. **Tremor is an orthogonal flag, as ALARM is in S3**: it can be set in `REST` or `SETTLING` (never in `FILTER_DRIVEN`) and it adds its offset to whatever base the state draws (E-IW-10, AC-IW-65), so a settle and a tremor are active together by construction.
487	
488	| State | Meaning | Entry | Exit | Who may cause it |
489	|---|---|---|---|---|
490	| `REST` | **at rest in time (IW-11 (b))**: no honest sample for `INSTR_REST_STEPS` Graph steps and no settle active; the needle sits on one pixel *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | initial; `INSTR_REST_STEPS` steps after the last honest sample once any ramp or settle has ended; on `hard_start`; on return to HONEST (the tremor flag does not affect `REST`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | the first honest sample (a ramp, or a settle if it passes the jump test); non-HONEST mode | (resting state) |
491	| `SETTLING` | closed-form settle in progress (IW-11) | a jump from rest while HONEST | `INSTR_SETTLE_MS` elapsed (to `REST`); re-based by another change (stays `SETTLING` with a fresh triple); non-HONEST mode (cleared at once) | the Graph (a real discrete change of the honest displayed value); the Filter (`motion_mode`) |
492	| `TREMOR` flag (orthogonal to `REST` and `SETTLING`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | honest stress tremor (IW-12) | predicate true while HONEST (onset ramp `TREMOR_ONSET_MS`) | predicate false (decay `TREMOR_DECAY_MS`, then the flag clears and the base state is unchanged); non-HONEST mode (cleared at once) | the Graph (the stress predicate from `read_view`: hazard-mode descriptors via `failures(filter)` (including an OVERLOAD descriptor on a cable of the bound loop component), and `stress_active` if granted); never Attention, sanity or a timer |
493	| `FILTER_DRIVEN` | `motion_mode` is GLIDE, TICK, STALE or RETURN; Instruments draw the received `displayed_pm` verbatim on the needle or meniscus (the Filter's trajectory, wander included, which never rests) and, on the card, the received digits (continuous tick, or the held digits of STALE) | the Filter's `motion_mode` leaves HONEST (the settle triple, tremor and notch are cleared that frame) | `motion_mode` returns to HONEST (CLEAR; discrepancy under `LEAK_EPS_DEG`, PF-12): to `REST`, no event, no flash | the Perception Filter only; Instruments never infer it |
494	
495	Reduced motion changes only how `SETTLING` and the `TREMOR` flag are drawn (a step and a held notch pair, IW-27); the states and their causes are the same.
496	
497	#### S3. ALARM flag
498	
499	`ALARM` is set while an `alarm_eligible` `FailureDescriptor` exists on the bound subject (read through `failures(filter)`, refreshed per Graph step) and cleared with it. It is orthogonal to every state above and to `motion_mode`: a lying needle never sets, moves or clears it. Only the Graph causes it (LS-13 fairness gate). It is drawn only on housings that carry the mark (IW-19) and never on the card.
500	
501	#### S4. Transitions
502	
503	| From | Event / guard | To | Notes |
504	|---|---|---|---|
505	| `DARK` | `lit(ref)` true | `LIT` | no dwell (EM-22) |
506	| `LIT` | `lit(ref)` false | `DARK` | an open card closes in the same render frame |
507	| `LIT` | `inspect` on a lit target (primary focus or secondary slot); no debounce gates the press *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | `CARD_OPEN` | the Adapter publishes `{inspect_card, ref}`; no command is submitted |
508	| `CARD_OPEN` | `inspect` again, or `cancel` (X) / B | `LIT` | |
509	| `CARD_OPEN` | `lit(ref)` false, reach lost, section transit, restore or `hard_start` | `DARK` / `LIT` per cause | immediate close; re-open needs a new press |
510	| `CARD_OPEN` | the Adapter context becomes `chart_table` (pause) or `chat`, or `loco_state` becomes STAGGERED, DOWNED, DEAD or IN_POD *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | `LIT` or `DARK` per `lit` | closes in the same render frame; not re-opened when the context returns to `gameplay` (E-IW-60); in co-op the overlay does not pause the sim, so the card never stays drawn under a modal |
511	| `CARD_OPEN` | movement intent past the dead-zone *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | `LIT` or `DARK` per `lit` | closes and the avatar moves in the same frame (IW-25, E-IW-29) |
512	| `CARD_OPEN` | binding lost | `DEAD` | card closes that frame |
513	| any | binding lost (node DESTROYED, SALVAGED or ABSENT; ref unresolvable) | `DEAD` | |
514	| `DEAD` | binding restored | `DARK` or `LIT` per `lit` | section re-load |
515	| `REST` | first honest sample whose accumulated change passes the jump test inside the window (IW-11 (b)) on a `settle_eligible` quantity *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | `SETTLING` | triple set *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
516	| `SETTLING` | any further change of the honest displayed value | `SETTLING` | re-based: `from` = value now drawn |
517	| any HONEST state (`REST` or `SETTLING`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | stress predicate true while HONEST | `TREMOR` flag set; the base state is unchanged | onset ramp; the drawn position is the base plus the tremor offset, clamped (E-IW-10) |
518	| `TREMOR` flag set | predicate false | flag cleared after the decay; base state unchanged | decay, then the needle rests on a pixel |
519	| any HONEST state | `motion_mode` becomes GLIDE, TICK, STALE or RETURN | `FILTER_DRIVEN` | triple, tremor and notch cleared that frame |

content.content:
The needle angle formula is defined as:

`a = clamp( ((T_c - t_sample) + tick_alpha) / GRAPH_STEP_TICKS, 0, 1 )`

`pm_honest = prev_honest_pm + (target_pm - prev_honest_pm) * a`

`pm_draw = pm_honest` (HONEST, no settle) `| settle_response(from_pm, to_pm, t_jump)` (HONEST, a jump, D.4) `| displayed_pm` (every other `motion_mode`, verbatim)

`theta(pm) = -arc_deg / 2 + pm * arc_deg / 1000` (degrees, clockwise from 12 o'clock)

`tip(pm) = round( pivot + needle_len_px * (sin theta, -cos theta) )` (whole art px, y down)

### D.5 Tremor (`tremor_offset`)

The tremor offset formula is defined as:

`s(t) = 0.6 * sin(2 * pi * f1 * t + phi1) + 0.4 * sin(2 * pi * f2 * t + phi2)`, `t = present_time`; `f_1 = 6.0 + 1.5 * u_1` (6.0 .. 7.5 Hz) and `f_2 = 9.0 + 1.0 * u_2` (9.0 .. 10.0 Hz), two **disjoint sub-bands** of the 6-10 Hz tremor band, so `f_2 - f_1` >= 1.5 Hz and the beat period is at most 0.67 s *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* (the earlier shared band let about 12 % of instruments draw near-equal frequencies and so long or permanent null windows with no tremor); `(u_i, phi_i)` from a presentation-local stateless hash of `(ref_key, i)`

`A_eff = max( TREMOR_AMP_PX, ceil( TREMOR_MIN_SCREEN_PX / k ) )`

`env(t) = min(1, (t - t_on) / TREMOR_ONSET_MS)` while `p_eff` holds; `env_off x max(0, 1 - (t - t_off) / TREMOR_DECAY_MS)` after it ends, with `env_off` = `env(t_off)` **latched at the instant the predicate ends** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (the earlier decay branch started from 1.0, so a predicate pulse that ended mid-onset jumped the envelope up to full before decaying); `p_eff = predicate OR (t - t_last_true) < TREMOR_HOLD_S`

`o = clamp( round( TREMOR_GAIN * A_eff * env * s(t) ), -A_eff, +A_eff )` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, **in frame-index space** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: `o` is a number of pre-rendered needle frames (OQ-IW-7: one frame index is one tip pixel along the arc, or one meniscus row of a LINEAR glass), and the drawn index is `idx_drawn = clamp( idx_base + o, 0, N_idx - 1 )` with `idx_base` the settle or ramp base index and `N_idx` the frame count of the sheet, so a non-zero `o` always moves the drawn tip by exactly `o` indices (the earlier tangent offset in art px could round to the same tip pixel on about 9 % of frames at 45 degrees) and the sum can never leave the end stops. The angular equivalent is `o x arc_deg / (N_idx - 1)` degrees

(The two-sine sum is wanted here: PF D.4 rejected it for the **wander** because a beat that dips to rest would break never-rest, whereas tremor has no never-rest duty and its irregularity is the point; a dip to rest between bursts reads as a real needle on a shaking hull.)

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TREMOR_F_MIN_HZ`, `TREMOR_F_MAX_HZ` | float Hz | 6 and 10 (named here from ART 7.3, not new) | art bible | the tremor band; disjoint from the Filter's 0.40-0.45 Hz wander; the two sines draw from the sub-bands 6.0-7.5 and 9.0-10.0 Hz inside it | *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)*
| `u_i`, `phi_i` | float | [0, 1), [0, 2 pi) | a presentation hash of `ref_key` (PF D.14 is the precedent; ADR candidate); **never** the kernel `rng_derive`, sim RNG is never used for presentation | per-instrument frequencies and phases, so two trembling gauges do not move in step |
| `TREMOR_AMP_PX` | int art px | 1 (ART 7.3 +-1), range 1-2 | this GDD | amplitude in art px |
| `TREMOR_MIN_SCREEN_PX` | int screen px | 2 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, range 2-3 | this GDD | the HR-12 floor applied to tremor |
| `k` | int | 1..`k_auto`+2 | PIPE zoom ladder | world scale |
| `TREMOR_GAIN` | float | 1.5 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, range 1.2-2.0 | this GDD | gain per unit of `A_eff` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: at `A_eff` 1, abs(o) = 1 when abs(s) >= 0.33; at `A_eff` 2, abs(o) = 1 when abs(s) >= 0.167 and 2 when abs(s) >= 0.5 |
| `TREMOR_ONSET_MS`, `TREMOR_DECAY_MS` | int ms | 150 (100-300), 600 (300-1000) `[PLACEHOLDER]` | this GDD | envelope; on a re-rise during a decay `t_on := t - env x TREMOR_ONSET_MS` so `env` stays continuous |
| `TREMOR_HOLD_S` | float s | 0 (range 0-1.0) `[PLACEHOLDER]` | this GDD | the playtest remedy if the predicate flaps at Graph-step rate |
| `predicate` | bool | | IW-12, refreshed per Graph step | true only while `motion_mode` is HONEST and a physical stress cause holds |

**Output Range:** `o` is an integer in [-`A_eff`, +`A_eff`]; 0 once the predicate has been false for `TREMOR_DECAY_MS`; exactly 0 in every non-HONEST frame. `A_eff` is 2 art px at `k` 1 and 1 art px at every `k` >= 2, so the offset is at least `TREMOR_MIN_SCREEN_PX` screen px at every rung *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* (reachable now that the gain scales with `A_eff`: the earlier unscaled gain reached 2 only at abs(s) = 1, so the k=1 tremor was effectively 1 px and the HR-12 floor claim was false). **Tremor and wander stay distinct:** wander peaks at 2 art px at 0.35-0.45 Hz, tremor at `A_eff` (1 art px at every `k` >= 2) at 6-10 Hz. At `k` 1 the peaks are equal (2 art px) and the cue is frequency and flip rate (tremor 12-20 tip flips per second against the wander's 4-6, VA-6); that is an accepted limitation of the zoom-out rung, recorded as OQ-IW-41. **Activity lint (`TREMOR_ACTIVITY`)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: measured on the **drawn tip index**, not on `o`: for every manifest `ref_key`, in any 2 s window at `env` 1, the drawn index changes between consecutive render frames at least `TREMOR_TIP_CHANGE_MIN_HZ` times per second (8 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, set by a measured sweep of the manifest `ref_key`s; the value must stay above the wander's 4-6 flips per second by a non-overlap margin, so the cue stays flip rate, OQ-IW-41) at `A_eff` 1 and at `A_eff` 2; a failing `ref_key` takes the next `tremor_salt` in its record. (The earlier lint counted frames with abs(o) >= 1, a worst case of 46 % at `A_eff` 1 and 62 % at `A_eff` 2 in a sweep of 4000 random draws; that measured `o`, which is not what the player sees, and it is replaced.) **Short pulse:** a predicate that holds for 100 ms and ends has `env_off` = 100 / `TREMOR_ONSET_MS` = 0.67, the decay runs from 0.67 and `env` never exceeds 0.67 (AC-IW-121).

**Example:** `ref_key` hashes give `f1` 7.2 Hz, `f2` 9.1 Hz, `phi` 0. At `k` 3, `A_eff` = max(1, ceil(2/3)) = 1; mid-stress (`env` 1) at t = 0.050 s: `s` = 0.6 sin(2.262) + 0.4 sin(2.859) = 0.6 x 0.7705 + 0.4 x 0.2790 = 0.574; `o` = clamp(round(1.5 x 0.574 = 0.86), -1, 1) = +1 px. At `k` 1, `A_eff` = 2 and `o` = clamp(round(1.5 x 2 x 0.574 = 1.72), -2, 2) = +2 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Decay: 300 ms after the predicate ends `env` = 0.5, so the product is at most 0.75 in magnitude and rounds to +-1 only when abs(s) >= 0.667, mostly 0; at 600 ms `env` = 0 and the needle rests on one pixel.

### D.6 Card scale, size and placement (`card_layout`)

**IW-26. Card parity: the same instrument, not a second one.**
*Rule.* The card uses the **same** `PerceptionRef` as its wall gauge (there is no card ref and no card lie), reads the same `Perceived` through the same memo, shows the same drawn value (it reads the instrument's own settle triple and tremor state), the same motion mode, the same gleam parameters and the same HR-5 tri-modal tell, from stage 1. A lie that starts, ends or changes while the card is open appears on the card in the same frame as on the wall gauge, with no flash of the true value. Closing and reopening a card on an active lie shows the same `Perceived` and plays no new sound (the sound is the Filter's request on the ref, not on the card). Opening the card never replay
===== In every non-HONEST mode the card needle draws 145043 1
ngle set as the wall needle (it must not be a more precise render of a lying value than the wall is of the same value). The card numeral is `displayed_value` of the **same** `.needle` ref's `Perceived` (checkpoint ruling C2): it is not a second lie target and carries no `lie_surface_id` of its own. In every non-HONEST mode the card needle draws `displayed_pm` verbatim (the Filter's trajectory, wander included, which never rests), while TICK (continuous tick) and STALE (held digits) govern the numeral only, so the card and the wall gauge never disagree about which motion mode is active (PF-9, PF-18, AC-PF-23; HR-14).
*Why.* Otherwise the card is either a free falsifier or a separate lie target.
*Edge notes.* The card has no module-frame surface, so if the wall shows a stage-3 `whole` frame

input.old_string: Honest tremor and the reduced-motion stress notch appear only on an honest reading (R9, R19), so "shake = real" is a rule the game never breaks.
input.new_string: Honest tremor and the reduced-motion stress notch are started only on an honest reading (R9, R19); a tremor already running at a lie's onset fades out through `tremor_weight_pm` over `TREMOR_BLEND_S` (PF-17), so "shake = real" still holds (a lie never starts a shake) and the onset second is never still, and the game never breaks the rule. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)*

input.old_string: a lying gauge that settles or trembles;
input.new_string: a lying gauge that settles or starts a tremor;

input.old_string: honest settle and tremor **only** when `motion_mode` is HONEST; the card is the same ref
input.new_string: honest settle and tremor **only** when `motion_mode` is HONEST **Accepted** with one amendment: PF-8/PF-17 as amended 2026-10-27 let an honest tremor already running at onset fade through `tremor_weight_pm` instead of stopping; the settle and the notch stop at once *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)*; the card is the same ref

input.old_string: | VA-6; settle and tremor only when `motion_mode` is HONEST |
input.new_string: | VA-6; settle is HONEST-only and a tremor is started only when `motion_mode` is HONEST (a running one fades by `tremor_weight_pm`) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)* |

input.old_string: Motion rules (before any number): settle and tremor only when `motion_mode` is HONEST;
input.new_string: Motion rules (before any number): settle is HONEST-only and a tremor is started only when `motion_mode` is HONEST (a running one fades by `tremor_weight_pm`) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)*;

input.old_string: | honest-only | tremor on a lying reading; tremor with no predicate |
input.new_string: | honest-only | a tremor started on a lying reading; tremor with no predicate *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)* |

input.old_string: starting no later than the glide | corruptible | any settle or tremor on the lying instrument; a sound-only lie |
input.new_string: starting no later than the glide; any tremor already running fades through `tremor_weight_pm` over `TREMOR_BLEND_S` | corruptible | any settle, or any new tremor, on the lying instrument; a tremor that stops dead at onset; a sound-only lie *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)* |

input.old_string: | never on a lying reading | none | absent when `motion_mode` is not HONEST |
input.new_string: | no new tremor or notch on a lying reading (a running tremor fades) | none | notch absent and tremor not startable when `motion_mode` is not HONEST *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)* |
